sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Caladbolg is the lightning sword of early Irish legend. A line of heroes once bore this blade. The noble Fergus mac Roch carried it with great fame. With his stroke he cut the tops from three hills in Meath. Commentary reads the weapon as a forerunner of Excalibur. The famous sword of King Arthur follows the same pattern. This blade takes its name from the words for the hard. It remains a bright sign of the old heroic age.

okr.objective: A lightning sword of the Irish hero Fergus mac Roich, seen as a forerunner of Excalibur.
key_results: Caladbolg was a lightning sword carried by several Irish heroes.
Fergus mac Roich used it to cut the tops off three hills in Meath.
Commentators read the blade as an anticipation of Excalibur.
